headline: Summit Access and Cog Railway Reservations
reservation: Book Cog Railway tickets separately. Driving your own eligible vehicle on the Mount Washington Auto Road does not require a reservation; pay at the Toll House. Check current road hours, vehicle restrictions, summit-facility hours, and the Higher Summits Forecast before departure.

days.title: The Highest Peak

stops.name: Mount Washington Summit
stops.detail: Visit the Sherman Adams Visitor Center and Tip-Top House to experience the extreme alpine environment.

stops.name: Mount Washington Auto Road
stops.detail: Drive the historic mountain road for expansive views of the Presidential Range.

days.driving: Allow 2 hours for the mountain ascent and descent; conditions vary.
days.note: Verify vehicle brake requirements and restrictions for the Auto Road before departure.

days.title: Notches and Waterfalls

stops.name: Glen Ellis Falls
stops.detail: Take the short walk to view this 64-foot waterfall dropping into the Ellis River.

stops.name: Pinkham Notch
stops.detail: Explore the base of the mountain and visit the AMC center for trail information and local history.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour for notch travel; conditions vary.
days.note: Waterfall paths can be slippery; stay on designated viewing platforms.

days.title: Crawford Notch Exploration

stops.name: Mount Washington Cog Railway
stops.detail: Experience the climb to the summit on the historic rack-and-pinion railway from the western side.

stops.name: Crawford Notch State Park
stops.detail: Drive through the dramatic mountain pass to view the steep granite cliffs.

days.driving: Allow 1.5 hours for valley transitions; conditions vary.
days.note: The Cog Railway and Auto Road are on opposite sides of the mountain; plan travel accordingly.

intel.title: Trailhead Pass Requirements
intel.text: Many trailheads in the White Mountain National Forest require a daily recreation pass. Look for self-service pay stations at Pinkham Notch and Crawford Notch parking areas.

intel.title: Mountain Shadows
intel.text: Cellular reception is highly unreliable in the deep notches and near the Cog Railway base. Carry paper maps if hiking or driving between Gorham and Bretton Woods.

intel.title: Village Fuel Points
intel.text: Refuel in North Conway or Gorham before heading into the notches. There are no fueling stations on the summit or along the immediate notch roads.

intel.title: Summit Wind Hazards
intel.text: Summit conditions can change from sun to freezing fog in minutes. Check the Mount Washington Observatory forecast before beginning any ascent, regardless of valley weather.

intel.title: Seasonal Road Closures
intel.text: The Auto Road and Cog Railway summit service are seasonal, typically operating from late spring to mid-autumn. Check official sites for precise opening and closing dates each year.

plan.arrival: Fly into Portland (PWM) or Boston, rent a car, and drive to a base in North Conway or Jackson to stock up on mountain layers.
plan.vehicle: A reliable car with good brakes is essential for the Auto Road; check the official site for specific transmission and vehicle length restrictions.
plan.goldenHour: Intervale Scenic Vista for sunset views of the White Mountains; cloud cover often dictates visibility.
